content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius

veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.
content.english: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

segments.t: Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.

content.latin: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
content.english: 18:3 Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.

segments.t: Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.

content.latin: 18:4 Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
content.english: 18:4 There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.

segments.t: Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.

content.latin: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: 18:5 Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: 18:6 In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
content.english: 18:6 He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,

segments.t: In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:

content.latin: 18:6 Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:
content.english: 18:6 Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * his going out is from the end of heaven,

segments.t: Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:

content.latin: 18:7 Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.
content.english: 18:7 And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.

segments.t: Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.

content.latin: 18:8 Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
content.english: 18:8 The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.

segments.t: Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.

content.latin: 18:9 Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
content.english: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

segments.t: Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.

content.latin: 18:10 Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.
content.english: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

segments.t: Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.

content.latin: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
content.english: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

segments.t: Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.

content.latin: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
content.english: 18:12 For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.

segments.t: Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.

content.latin: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
content.english: 18:13 Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.

segments.t: Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.

content.latin: 18:14 Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
content.english: 18:14 If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.

segments.t: Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.

content.latin: 18:15 Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
content.english: 18:15 And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.

segments.t: Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.

content.latin: 18:15 Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
content.english: 18:15 O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.

segments.t: Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.

content.latin: Psalmus 33 [2]
content.english: Psalm 33 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 33

content.latin: 33:2 Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.
content.english: 33:2 I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.

segments.t: Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.

content.latin: 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
content.english: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

segments.t: In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.

content.latin: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.
content.english: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

segments.t: Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.

content.latin: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
content.english: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

segments.t: Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.

content.latin: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
content.english: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

segments.t: Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.

content.latin: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.
content.english: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

segments.t: Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.

content.latin: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
content.english: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

segments.t: Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.

content.latin: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
content.english: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

segments.t: Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.

content.latin: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
content.english: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

segments.t: Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.

content.latin: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
content.english: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

segments.t: Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.

content.latin: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
content.english: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

segments.t: Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.

content.latin: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
content.english: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

segments.t: Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?

content.latin: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
content.english: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

segments.t: Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.

content.latin: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
content.english: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

segments.t: Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.

content.latin: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.
content.english: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

segments.t: Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.

content.latin: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
content.english: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

segments.t: Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.

content.latin: 33:18 Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

segments.t: Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.

content.latin: 33:19 Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
content.english: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

segments.t: Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.

content.latin: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
content.english: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

segments.t: Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.

content.latin: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
content.english: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

segments.t: Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.

content.latin: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.
content.english: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

segments.t: Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.

content.latin: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
content.english: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

segments.t: Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.

content.english: Psalm 44 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

segments.t: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

segments.t: Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

segments.t: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

segments.t: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

segments.t: Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

segments.t: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

segments.t: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

segments.t: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth. They shall remember thy name, O Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.

content.latin: ℣. In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.
content.english: ℣. Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth:

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: ℟. And their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: De Epístola prima beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Corínthios
content.english: Lesson from the first letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

content.latin: 1 Sic nos exístimet homo ut minístros Christi, et dispensatóres mysteriórum Dei.
content.english: 1 Let a man so account of us as of the ministers of Christ, and the dispensers of the mysteries of God.

segments.t: Sic nos exístimet homo ut minístros Christi, et dispensatóres mysteriórum Dei.

content.latin: 2 Hic iam quǽritur inter dispensatóres ut fidélis quis inveniátur.
content.english: 2 Here now it is required among the dispensers, that a man be found faithful.

segments.t: Hic iam quǽritur inter dispensatóres ut fidélis quis inveniátur.

content.latin: 3 Mihi autem pro mínimo est ut a vobis iúdicer, aut ab humáno die: sed neque meípsum iúdico.
content.english: 3 But to me it is a very small thing to be judged by you, or by man's day; but neither do I judge my own self.

segments.t: Mihi autem pro mínimo est ut a vobis iúdicer, aut ab humáno die: sed neque meípsum iúdico.

content.latin: 4 Nihil enim mihi cónscius sum, sed non in hoc iustificátus sum: qui autem iúdicat me, Dóminus est.
content.english: 4 For I am not conscious to myself of any thing, yet am I not hereby justified; but he that judgeth me, is the Lord.

segments.t: Nihil enim mihi cónscius sum, sed non in hoc iustificátus sum: qui autem iúdicat me, Dóminus est.

content.latin: 5 Ítaque nolíte ante tempus iudicáre, quoadúsque véniat Dóminus: qui et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit consília córdium: et tunc laus erit unicuíque a Deo.
content.english: 5 Therefore judge not before the time; until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts; and then shall every man have praise from God.

segments.t: Ítaque nolíte ante tempus iudicáre, quoadúsque véniat Dóminus: qui et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit consília córdium: et tunc laus erit unicuíque a Deo.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus:
content.english: ℟. Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves, said the Lord:

segments.t: Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus:

content.latin: * Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.
content.english: * Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.

content.latin: ℣. Dum lucem habétis, crédite in lucem, ut fílii lucis sitis.
content.english: ℣. Whilst you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be the children of light.

segments.t: Dum lucem habétis, crédite in lucem, ut fílii lucis sitis.

content.latin: ℟. Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.
content.english: ℟. Be ye therefore wise as serpents and simple as doves.

segments.t: Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 6 Hæc autem, fratres, transfigurávi in me et Apóllo, propter vos: ut in nobis discátis, ne supra quam scriptum est, unus advérsus álterum inflétur pro álio.
content.english: 6 But these things, brethren, I have in a figure transferred to myself and to Apollo, for your sakes; that in us you may learn, that one be not puffed up against the other for another, above that which is written.

segments.t: Hæc autem, fratres, transfigurávi in me et Apóllo, propter vos: ut in nobis discátis, ne supra quam scriptum est, unus advérsus álterum inflétur pro álio.

content.latin: 7 Quis enim te discérnit? Quid autem habes quod non accepísti? Si autem accepísti, quid gloriáris quasi non accéperis?
content.english: 7 For who distinguisheth thee? Or what hast thou that thou hast not received? And if thou hast received, why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received it?

segments.t: Quis enim te discérnit? Quid autem habes quod non accepísti? Si autem accepísti, quid gloriáris quasi non accéperis?

content.latin: 8 Iam saturáti estis, iam dívites facti estis: sine nobis regnátis: et útinam regnétis, ut et nos vobíscum regnémus.
content.english: 8 You are now full; you are now become rich; you reign without us; and I would to God you did reign, that we also might reign with you.

segments.t: Iam saturáti estis, iam dívites facti estis: sine nobis regnátis: et útinam regnétis, ut et nos vobíscum regnémus.

content.latin: 9 Puto enim quod Deus nos Apóstolos novíssimos osténdit, tamquam morti destinátos: quia spectáculum facti sumus mundo, et Ángelis, et homínibus.
content.english: 9 For I think that God hath set forth us apostles, the last, as it were men appointed to death: we are made a spectacle to the world, and to angels, and to men.

segments.t: Puto enim quod Deus nos Apóstolos novíssimos osténdit, tamquam morti destinátos: quia spectáculum facti sumus mundo, et Ángelis, et homínibus.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Tóllite iugum meum super vos, dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde:
content.english: ℟. Take up my yoke upon you, said the Lord, and learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart.

segments.t: Tóllite iugum meum super vos, dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde:

content.latin: * Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.
content.english: * For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

content.latin: ℣. Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris.
content.english: ℣. And you shall find rest to your souls.

segments.t: Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris.

content.latin: ℟. Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.
content.english: ℟. For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

segments.t: Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 10 Nos stulti propter Christum, vos autem prudéntes in Christo: nos infírmi, vos autem fortes: vos nóbiles, nos autem ignóbiles.
content.english: 10 We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honourable, but we without honour.

segments.t: Nos stulti propter Christum, vos autem prudéntes in Christo: nos infírmi, vos autem fortes: vos nóbiles, nos autem ignóbiles.

content.latin: 11 Usque in hanc horam et esurímus, et sitímus, et nudi sumus, et cólaphis cǽdimur, et instábiles sumus,
content.english: 11 Even unto this hour we both hunger and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no fixed abode;

segments.t: Usque in hanc horam et esurímus, et sitímus, et nudi sumus, et cólaphis cǽdimur, et instábiles sumus,

content.latin: 12 Et laborámus operántes mánibus nostris: maledícimur, et benedícimus: persecutiónem pátimur, et sustinémus:
content.english: 12 And we labour, working with our own hands: we are reviled, and we bless; we are persecuted, and we suffer it.

segments.t: Et laborámus operántes mánibus nostris: maledícimur, et benedícimus: persecutiónem pátimur, et sustinémus:

content.latin: 13 Blasphemámur, et obsecrámus: tamquam purgaménta huius mundi facti sumus, ómnium peripséma usque adhuc.
content.english: 13 We are blasphemed, and we entreat; we are made as the refuse of this world, the offscouring of all even until now.

segments.t: Blasphemámur, et obsecrámus: tamquam purgaménta huius mundi facti sumus, ómnium peripséma usque adhuc.

content.latin: 14 Non ut confúndam vos, hæc scribo, sed ut fílios meos caríssimos móneo.
content.english: 14 I write not these things to confound you; but I admonish you as my dearest children.

segments.t: Non ut confúndam vos, hæc scribo, sed ut fílios meos caríssimos móneo.

content.latin: 15 Nam si decem míllia pædagogórum habeátis in Christo, sed non multos patres, nam in Christo Iesu per Evangélium ego vos génui.
content.english: 15 For if you have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet not many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you.

segments.t: Nam si decem míllia pædagogórum habeátis in Christo, sed non multos patres, nam in Christo Iesu per Evangélium ego vos génui.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo aut quid loquámini:
content.english: ℟. But when they shall deliver you up to the judges, take no thought how or what to speak:

segments.t: Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo aut quid loquámini:

content.latin: * Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
content.english: * for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak:

content.latin: ℣. Non enim vos estis qui loquímini: sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis.
content.english: ℣. For it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.

segments.t: Non enim vos estis qui loquímini: sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis.

content.latin: ℟. Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
content.english: ℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

segments.t: Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
content.english: ℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

segments.t: Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.

content.latin: Nocturnus II
content.english: Nocturn II

segments.t: Nocturnus II

content.latin: Ant. Príncipes populórum * congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham.
content.english: Ant. The princes of the people * are gathered together, with the God of Abraham.

segments.t: Ant.
Príncipes populórum * congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham.

content.latin: Psalmus 46 [4]
content.english: Psalm 46 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 46

content.latin: 46:2 Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * iubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.
content.english: 46:2 O clap your hands, all ye nations: * shout unto God with the voice of joy,

segments.t: Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * iubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.

content.latin: 46:3 Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.
content.english: 46:3 For the Lord is high, terrible: * a great king over all the earth.

segments.t: Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.

content.english: 46:4 He hath subdued the people under us; * and the nations under our feet.

content.latin: Iacóbus, Zebedǽi fílius, Ioánnis Apóstoli germánus frater, Galilǽus, inter primos Apóstolos vocátus cum fratre, relíctis patre ac rétibus, secútus est Dóminum, et ambo ab ipso Iesu Boanérges, id est, tonítrui fílii sunt appelláti. Is unus fuit ex tribus Apóstolis, quos Salvátor máxime diléxit, et testes esse vóluit suæ transfiguratiónis, et interésse miráculo cum archisynagógi fíliam a mórtuis excitávit, et adésse cum secéssit in montem Olivéti, Patrem oratúrus, ántequam a Iudǽis comprehenderétur.
content.english: James, the Son of Zebedee and brother of the Apostle John, was a Galilean, and with his brother one of the first of His Apostles whom the Lord called, whileas they were in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets and they immediately left the ship, and their father, and followed Him. Matth. iv. 21, 22. And He surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder. Mark iii. 17. Peter, and James, and John, were the three Apostles whom the Saviour loved best; them He took and brought up into an high mountain apart, and was transfigured before them, Matth. xvii. 1,2; when He went to the house of the ruler of the synagogue to raise his daughter from the dead, He suffered no man to follow Him save Peter, and James, and John, Mark v. 37; and, at the last, just before the Jews took Him, when He cometh unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples: Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder. He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee. Matth. xxvi. 36, 37.

content.latin: Post Iesu Christi ascénsum in cælum, in Iudǽa et Samaría eius divinitátem prǽdicans, plúrimos ad christiánam fidem perdúxit. Mox in Hispániam proféctus, ibi áliquos ad Christum convértit; ex quorum número septem póstea epíscopi a beáto Petro ordináti in Hispániam primi dirécti sunt. Deínde Ierosólymam revérsus, cum inter álios Hermógenem magum fídei veritáte imbuísset, Heródes Agríppa Cláudio imperatóre ad regnum elátus ut a Iudǽis grátiam iníret, Iacóbum líbere Iesum Christum Deum confiténtem cápitis condemnávit. Quem cum is, qui eum dúxerat ad tribúnal, fórtiter martýrium subeúntem vidísset, statim se et ipse Christiánum esse proféssus est.
content.english: After that Jesus Christ was ascended into heaven, James preached how that He was God, and led many in Judaea and Samaria to the Christian Faith. A while afterward, he went to Spain, and there he brought some to Christ, of whom seven were afterwards ordained Bishops by Blessed Peter, and were the first such sent into that country. From Spain James went back to Jerusalem, where he taught the Faith to diverse persons, and, among others, to the Magician Hermogenes. Thereupon Herod Agrippa, who had been raised to the kingdom under the Emperor Claudius, to curry favour with the Jews, condemned James to death for his firm confession that Jesus Christ is God. The officer who led James to the judgment-seat, at sight of the courage wherewith he was ready to offer up his testimony, declared himself also to be a Christian.

content.latin: Ad supplícium cum raperéntur, pétiit ille a Iacóbo véniam; quem Iacóbus osculátus, Pax, inquit, tibi sit. Itaque utérque est secúri percússus, cum paulo ante Iacóbus paralýticum sanásset. Corpus eius póstea Compostéllam translátum est, ubi summa celebritáte cólitur, conveniéntibus eo religiónis et voti causa ex toto terrárum orbe peregrínis. Memória ipsíus natális hodiérno die, qui translatiónis dies est, ab Ecclésia celebrátur, cum ipse circa festum Paschæ, primus Apostolórum Ierosólymis profúso sánguine testimónium Iesu Christo déderit.
content.english: As they were being hurried to execution, this man asked pardon of James, and the Apostle kissed him, saying, Peace be unto thee. James healed a paralytic, and immediately afterwards both the prisoners were beheaded. The body of the Apostle was afterwards taken to Compostella, (in the province of Galicia, in Spain,) where his grave is very famous. Multitudes of pilgrims from all parts of the earth betake themselves thither to pray, out of sheer piety or in fulfilment of vows. The Birthday of James is kept by the Church upon this day, which is that of the bringing of his body to Compostella. It was about Easter-time Acts xii. 2-4 that he bore witness to Jesus Christ with his blood, at Jerusalem, being the first of the Apostles to do so.

content.latin: Non turbétur quisquam, si ádeo imperféctos dícimus Apóstolos fuísse; nondum enim mystérium crucis erat consummátum, nondum grátia Spíritus in corda ipsórum infúsa. Quod si virtútem ipsórum díscere cupis, quales post datam grátiam Spíritus fúerint, consídera, et vidébis omnem ab illis pervérsam affectiónem fuísse superátam. Hac enim de causa eórum modo imperféctio revelátur, ut apérte percípere possis quales súbito per grátiam effécti fuérunt. Quod ígitur nihil spiritále petébant nec de cælésti regno quidquam cogitábant, perspícuum est. Sed tamen inspiciámus étiam quómodo accédant et quid dicant. Vólumus, ínquiunt, ut, quodcúmque petiérimus, fácias nobis. Ad quod Christus, Quid vultis? respóndit: non ignórans certe, sed ut eos respondére cogat et ulcus détegat, et ita medicaméntum appónat.
content.english: Let no man be troubled if we say that the Apostles were still imperfect, for the mystery of the Cross was not yet finished, the grace of the Spirit had not yet been shed abroad in their hearts. If thou wilt behold them in their strength, consider them such as they became after the grace of the Spirit was given them, and thou wilt perceive that they had trodden under foot every vain desire. This is the cause wherefore their present imperfection is made known unto us, that is, that thou mayest see how great a change could be forthwith wrought by grace. But nevertheless let us now look how they came unto Christ, and what they said. Master, they said, we would that Thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire. Mark x. 35. And He said unto them: What would ye that I should do for you? Mark X. 36. not, surely, that He knew not what their wish was, but that He would make them answer, and so uncover the wound, to lay a plaster upon it.

content.latin: Illi vero, cum erubéscerent et verecúndia prohiberéntur, quóniam humáno afféctu eo devénerant, seórsum ab áliis discípulis Christum accipiéntes, interrogavérunt. Progréssi sunt enim, inquit, ne illis manifésti fíerent; et ita demum ea quæ volébant, dixérunt. Volébant autem, ut ego conício, quóniam super duódecim sedes sessúros discípulos audiérunt, primátum huius conséssus impetráre: et præpóni quidem se céteris sciébant; Petrum vero sibi præférri formidántes, dícere ausi sunt: Dic ut unus a dextris, alter a sinístris sédeat. Et urgent dicéntes: Dic. Quid ígitur ipse? Ut significáret eos nihil pétere spiritále, sed nec scire quidem quid póstulent, non enim pétere audérent, si scirent. Nescítis, ait, quid petátis: nescítis quam magnum hoc sit, quam mirábile ac ipsas superióres excédens virtútes.
content.english: Their wish proceeded from earthly motives, and they were shy and ashamed to express it, and therefore they took Christ apart, and so asked Him. The Evangelist saith: For they were gone apart, that they might not be discovered of them and then they told Him what they sought. To me it seemeth most likely that they had heard how that the disciples should sit upon twelve thrones; they were fain to obtain for themselves the chiefest places at this enthronement; they knew that the Lord loved them better than the most of the others; but they feared that Peter would still be preferred before them; and therefore they made bold to say: Grant unto us that we may sit, one at thy right Hand, and the other at thy left Hand, in thy glory. Mark x. 37. They were even instant with Him, saying: Say that we may. And what answered He? To show that they were asking no spiritual gift, nor even knew for themselves what they were asking, nor would have asked it if they had known what it was, Jesus said unto them: Ye know not what ye ask, ye know not how great a thing, how wonderful a thing this is, a thing which even is not Mine to give.

content.latin: Et adiécit: Potéstis bíbere cálicem, quem ego bibitúrus sum; et baptísmo, quo ego baptízor, baptizári? Perpéndis quómodo statim ab hac opinióne ipsos remóvit, contrária eis dísserens. Nam vos, inquit, de honóribus et de corónis mecum ágitis; ego vero de luctámine atque sudóre díssero. Non præmiórum hoc tempus est, nec illa glória mea modo apparébit; sed cædis ac periculórum tempus præsens est. Pérspice autem quáliter ipso interrogatiónis modo et hortátur et állicit. Non enim dixit: Potestísne cædem subíre, potestísne vestrum effúndere sánguinem? Sed, Quonam pacto potéstis bíbere cálicem? Deínde allíciens, inquit, Quem ego bibitúrus sum; ut ipsa cum eo communicatióne labórum promptióres redderéntur.
content.english: And He said moreover: Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? Behold how He turneth their thoughts at once another way, speaking to them of things altogether different, as though He said, Ye come unto Me treating of honours and crowns, but I speak unto you of the wrestling and the sweat. This is not yet the time of reward, neither is My glory immediately to be revealed; but now death and danger are present with you. But consider how, by the manner of His questioning, He doth both exhort and invite them. He saith not Are ye able to bear death? Are ye able to shed your blood? but: How are ye able to drink the cup whereto He presently inviteth them, saying: the cup that I shall drink of; that He may make them readier for the strife by knowing that it is a strife which they are to share with Him.

content.latin: Esto, Dómine, plebi tuæ sanctificátor et custos: ut, Apóstoli tui Iacóbi muníta præsídiis, et conversatióne tibi pláceat, et secúra mente desérviat.
content.english: Be Thou thyself, O Lord, the Sanctifier and the Shepherd of thy people, that we who are overshadowed by the help of thine Apostle James may, in our conversation, walk with thee, and in all quietness of spirit serve thee.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: Ant. Qui odit ánimam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam custódit eam.

content.latin: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui beáti Christóphori Mártyris tui natalítia cólimus, intercessióne eius in tui nóminis amóre roborémur.
content.english: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that we who celebrate the martyrdom of blessed Christopher, through his intercession be strengthened in your love.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Iam lucis orto sídere,
content.english: Now in the sun's new dawning ray,

content.latin: Deum precémur súpplices,
content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: Ipsi canámus glóriam.
content.english: May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

content.latin: Deo Patri sit glória,
content.english: All laud to God the Father be,

content.latin: Eiúsque soli Fílio,
content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.latin: Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
content.english: To God the holy Paraclete.

content.english: Amen.

Psalmus 93(1-11)

content.latin: 93:1 Deus ultiónum Dóminus: * Deus ultiónum líbere egit.
content.english: 93:1 The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth: * the God of revenge hath acted freely.

segments.t: Deus ultiónum Dóminus: * Deus ultiónum líbere egit.

content.latin: 93:2 Exaltáre, qui iúdicas terram: * redde retributiónem supérbis.
content.english: 93:2 Lift up thyself, thou that judgest the earth: * render a reward to the proud.

segments.t: Exaltáre, qui iúdicas terram: * redde retributiónem supérbis.

content.latin: 93:3 Úsquequo peccatóres, Dómine, * úsquequo peccatóres gloriabúntur:
content.english: 93:3 How long shall sinners, O Lord: * how long shall sinners glory?

segments.t: Úsquequo peccatóres, Dómine, * úsquequo peccatóres gloriabúntur:

content.latin: 93:4 Effabúntur, et loquéntur iniquitátem: * loquéntur omnes, qui operántur iniustítiam?
content.english: 93:4 Shall they utter, and speak iniquity: * shall all speak who work injustice?

segments.t: Effabúntur, et loquéntur iniquitátem: * loquéntur omnes, qui operántur iniustítiam?

content.latin: 93:5 Pópulum tuum, Dómine, humiliavérunt: * et hereditátem tuam vexavérunt.
content.english: 93:5 Thy people, O Lord, they have brought low: * and they have afflicted thy inheritance.

segments.t: Pópulum tuum, Dómine, humiliavérunt: * et hereditátem tuam vexavérunt.

content.latin: 93:6 Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt: * et pupíllos occidérunt.
content.english: 93:6 They have slain the widow and the stranger: * and they have murdered the fatherless.

segments.t: Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt: * et pupíllos occidérunt.

content.latin: 93:7 Et dixérunt: Non vidébit Dóminus, * nec intélleget Deus Iacob.
content.english: 93:7 And they have said: The Lord shall not see: * neither shall the God of Jacob understand.

segments.t: Et dixérunt: Non vidébit Dóminus, * nec intélleget Deus Iacob.

content.latin: 93:8 Intellégite, insipiéntes in pópulo: * et stulti, aliquándo sápite.
content.english: 93:8 Understand, ye senseless among the people: * and, you fools, be wise at last.

segments.t: Intellégite, insipiéntes in pópulo: * et stulti, aliquándo sápite.

content.latin: 93:9 Qui plantávit aurem, non áudiet? * aut qui finxit óculum, non consíderat?
content.english: 93:9 He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? * or he that formed the eye, doth he not consider?

segments.t: Qui plantávit aurem, non áudiet? * aut qui finxit óculum, non consíderat?

content.latin: 93:10 Qui córripit gentes, non árguet: * qui docet hóminem sciéntiam?
content.english: 93:10 He that chastiseth nations, shall he not rebuke: * he that teacheth man knowledge?

segments.t: Qui córripit gentes, non árguet: * qui docet hóminem sciéntiam?

content.latin: 93:11 Dóminus scit cogitatiónes hóminum, * quóniam vanæ sunt.
content.english: 93:11 The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men, * that they are vain.

segments.t: Dóminus scit cogitatiónes hóminum, * quóniam vanæ sunt.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

Psalmus 93(12-23)

content.latin: 93:12 Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine: * et de lege tua docúeris eum,
content.english: 93:12 Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord: * and shalt teach him out of thy law.

segments.t: Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine: * et de lege tua docúeris eum,

content.latin: 93:13 Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis: * donec fodiátur peccatóri fóvea.
content.english: 93:13 That thou mayst give him rest from the evil days: * till a pit be dug for the wicked.

segments.t: Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis: * donec fodiátur peccatóri fóvea.

content.latin: 93:14 Quia non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: * et hereditátem suam non derelínquet.
content.english: 93:14 For the Lord will not cast off his people: * neither will he forsake his own inheritance.

segments.t: Quia non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: * et hereditátem suam non derelínquet.

content.latin: 93:15 Quoadúsque iustítia convertátur in iudícium: * et qui iuxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde.
content.english: 93:15 Until justice be turned into judgment: * and they that are near it are all the upright in heart.

segments.t: Quoadúsque iustítia convertátur in iudícium: * et qui iuxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde.

content.latin: 93:16 Quis consúrget mihi advérsus malignántes? * aut quis stabit mecum advérsus operántes iniquitátem?
content.english: 93:16 Who shall rise up for me against the evildoers? * or who shall stand with me against the workers of iniquity?

segments.t: Quis consúrget mihi advérsus malignántes? * aut quis stabit mecum advérsus operántes iniquitátem?

content.latin: 93:17 Nisi quia Dóminus adiúvit me: * paulo minus habitásset in inférno ánima mea.
content.english: 93:17 Unless the Lord had been my helper, * my soul had almost dwelt in hell.

segments.t: Nisi quia Dóminus adiúvit me: * paulo minus habitásset in inférno ánima mea.

content.latin: 93:18 Si dicébam: Motus est pes meus: * misericórdia tua, Dómine, adiuvábat me.
content.english: 93:18 If I said: My foot is moved: * thy mercy, O Lord, assisted me.

segments.t: Si dicébam: Motus est pes meus: * misericórdia tua, Dómine, adiuvábat me.

content.latin: 93:19 Secúndum multitúdinem dolórum meórum in corde meo: * consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.
content.english: 93:19 According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, * thy comforts have given joy to my soul.

segments.t: Secúndum multitúdinem dolórum meórum in corde meo: * consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.

content.latin: 93:20 Numquid adhǽret tibi sedes iniquitátis: * qui fingis labórem in præcépto?
content.english: 93:20 Doth the seat of iniquity stick to thee, * who framest labour in commandment?

segments.t: Numquid adhǽret tibi sedes iniquitátis: * qui fingis labórem in præcépto?

content.latin: 93:21 Captábunt in ánimam iusti: * et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.
content.english: 93:21 They will hunt after the soul of the just, * and will condemn innocent blood.

segments.t: Captábunt in ánimam iusti: * et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.

content.latin: 93:22 Et factus est mihi Dóminus in refúgium: * et Deus meus in adiutórium spei meæ.
content.english: 93:22 But the Lord is my refuge: * and my God the help of my hope.

segments.t: Et factus est mihi Dóminus in refúgium: * et Deus meus in adiutórium spei meæ.

content.latin: 93:23 Et reddet illis iniquitátem ipsórum: et in malítia eórum dispérdet eos: * dispérdet illos Dóminus, Deus noster.
content.english: 93:23 And he will render them their iniquity: and in their malice he will destroy them: * the Lord our God will destroy them.

segments.t: Et reddet illis iniquitátem ipsórum: et in malítia eórum dispérdet eos: * dispérdet illos Dóminus, Deus noster.

content.english: Psalm 107 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 107

content.latin: 107:2 Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psallam in glória mea.
content.english: 107:2 My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and will give praise, with my glory.

segments.t: Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psallam in glória mea.

content.latin: 107:3 Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
content.english: 107:3 Arise, my glory; arise, psaltery and harp * I will arise in the morning early.

segments.t: Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.

content.latin: 107:4 Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psallam tibi in natiónibus.
content.english: 107:4 I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: * and I will sing unto thee among the nations.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psallam tibi in natiónibus.

content.latin: 107:5 Quia magna est super cælos misericórdia tua: * et usque ad nubes véritas tua:
content.english: 107:5 For thy mercy is great above the heavens: * and thy truth even unto the clouds.

segments.t: Quia magna est super cælos misericórdia tua: * et usque ad nubes véritas tua:

content.latin: 107:6 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram glória tua: * ut liberéntur dilécti tui.
content.english: 107:6 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and thy glory over all the earth: * that thy beloved may be delivered.

segments.t: Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram glória tua: * ut liberéntur dilécti tui.

content.latin: 107:7 Salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me: * Deus locútus est in sancto suo:
content.english: 107:7 Save with thy right hand and hear me. * God hath spoken in his holiness.

segments.t: Salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me: * Deus locútus est in sancto suo:

content.latin: 107:8 Exsultábo, et dívidam Síchimam, * et convállem tabernaculórum dimétiar.
content.english: 107:8 I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem * and I will mete out the vale of tabernacles.

segments.t: Exsultábo, et dívidam Síchimam, * et convállem tabernaculórum dimétiar.

content.latin: 107:9 Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim suscéptio cápitis mei.
content.english: 107:9 Galaad is mine: and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim the protection of my head.

segments.t: Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim suscéptio cápitis mei.

content.latin: 107:10 Iuda rex meus: * Moab lebes spei meæ.
content.english: 107:10 Juda is my king: * Moab the pot of my hope.

segments.t: Iuda rex meus: * Moab lebes spei meæ.

content.latin: 107:10 In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ amíci facti sunt.
content.english: 107:10 Over Edom I will stretch out my shoe: * the aliens are become my friends.

segments.t: In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ amíci facti sunt.

content.latin: 107:11 Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
content.english: 107:11 Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?

segments.t: Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?

content.latin: 107:12 Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos, * et non exíbis, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
content.english: 107:12 Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our armies?

segments.t: Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos, * et non exíbis, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?

content.latin: 107:13 Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
content.english: 107:13 O grant us help from trouble: * for vain is the help of man.

segments.t: Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.

content.latin: 107:14 In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet inimícos nostros.
content.english: 107:14 Through God we shall do mightily: * and he will bring our enemies to nothing.

segments.t: In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet inimícos nostros.

content.latin: Dómine Deus omnípotens, qui ad princípium huius diéi nos perveníre fecísti: tua nos hódie salva virtúte; ut in hac die ad nullum declinémus peccátum, sed semper ad tuam iustítiam faciéndam nostra procédant elóquia, dirigántur cogitatiónes et ópera.
content.english: O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who has safely brought us to the beginning of this day: defend us by thy mighty power; and grant that this day we fall into no sin, but that all our doings may be ordered by thy governance, to do always what is righteous in thy sight.

content.latin: Philíppis, in Macedónia, natális sancti Erásti, qui, illic a beáto Paulo Apóstolo relíctus Epíscopus, ibídem martýrio coronátus est.
content.english: On the same 26th day of July, was also born into the better life: At Philippi, in Macedonia, holy Erastus, who was left there as Bishop by the blessed Apostle Paul, and was there crowned with martyrdom.

content.latin: Romæ, via Latína, sanctórum Mártyrum Symphrónii, Olýmpii, Theodúli et Exsupériæ; qui (ut in gestis sancti Stéphani Papæ légitur), ígnibus combústi, martýrii palmam adépti sunt.
content.english: At Rome, upon the Latin Way, the holy martyrs Symphronius, Olympius, Theodulus, and Exuperia, who, as is written in the Acts of the holy Pope Stephen I, were burnt in the fire, and so gained the palm of martyrdom.

content.latin: In Portu Románo sancti Hyacínthi Mártyris, qui, primo in ignem iniéctus, deínde in profluéntem præcipitátus, illǽsus evásit; post hæc, sub Traiáno Imperatóre, a Leóntio Consulári percússus gládio, vitam finívit. Ipsíus corpus Iúlia Matróna in prǽdio suo, iuxta Urbem, sepelívit.
content.english: At Porto Romano, the holy martyr Hyacinth. He was first cast into the fire, and then into a torrent, but escaped unhurt. Afterwards, under the Emperor Trajan, Leontius the Consular caused him to be smitten with the sword, and so ended his earthly life. The matron Julia buried his body upon her own farm hard by the city of Rome.

content.latin: Verónæ sancti Valéntis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
content.english: Also at Rome, [in the second century,] the holy Priest Pastor, who giveth his name to the Church upon the Viminal Hill, which is that of holy Pudentiana.

content.latin: In monastério sancti Benedícti, in agro Mantuáno, sancti Simeónis, Mónachi et Eremítæ, qui, multis miráculis clarus, in senectúte bona quiévit.
content.english: In the monastery of St Benedict, in the country of Mantua, [in the year 1016,] the holy Monk and Hermit Simeon, who fell asleep in a good old age, famous for many marvels.

content.latin: 101:2 Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: 101:2 Hear, O Lord, my prayer: * and let my cry come to thee.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: 101:3 Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.
content.english: 101:3 Turn not away thy face from me: * in the day when I am in trouble, incline thy ear to me.

segments.t: Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.

content.latin: 101:3 In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.
content.english: 101:3 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * hear me speedily.

segments.t: In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.

content.latin: 101:4 Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.
content.english: 101:4 For my days are vanished like smoke: * and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire.

segments.t: Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.

content.latin: 101:5 Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.
content.english: 101:5 I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered: * because I forgot to eat my bread.

segments.t: Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.

content.latin: 101:6 A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.
content.english: 101:6 Through the voice of my groaning, * my bone hath cleaved to my flesh.

segments.t: A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.

content.latin: 101:7 Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.
content.english: 101:7 I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness: * I am like a night raven in the house.

segments.t: Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.

content.latin: 101:8 Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.
content.english: 101:8 I have watched, * and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop.

segments.t: Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.

content.latin: 101:9 Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.
content.english: 101:9 All the day long my enemies reproached me: * and they that praised me did swear against me.

segments.t: Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.

content.latin: 101:10 Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.
content.english: 101:10 For I did eat ashes like bread, * and mingled my drink with weeping.

segments.t: Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.

content.latin: 101:11 A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.
content.english: 101:11 Because of thy anger and indignation: * for having lifted me up thou hast thrown me down.

segments.t: A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.

content.latin: 101:12 Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.
content.english: 101:12 My days have declined like a shadow, * and I am withered like grass.

segments.t: Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.

content.latin: 101:13 Tu autem, Dómine, in ætérnum pérmanes: * et memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, in ætérnum pérmanes: * et memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.

segments.t: Tu exsúrgens miseréberis Sion: * quia tempus miseréndi eius, quia venit tempus.

content.latin: 101:15 Quóniam placuérunt servis tuis lápides eius: * et terræ eius miserebúntur.

content.latin: 101:16 Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.
content.english: 101:16 And the Gentiles shall fear thy name, O Lord, * and all the kings of the earth thy glory.

segments.t: Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 101:17 Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.

segments.t: Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.

content.latin: 101:18 Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.

segments.t: Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.

content.latin: 101:19 Scribántur hæc in generatióne áltera: * et pópulus, qui creábitur, laudábit Dóminum:

content.latin: 101:22 Ut annúntient in Sion nomen Dómini: * et laudem eius in Ierúsalem.

Psalmus 101(24-29)

content.latin: 101:24 Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.
content.english: 101:24 He answered him in the way of his strength: * Declare unto me the fewness of my days.

segments.t: Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.

content.latin: 101:25 Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.
content.english: 101:25 Call me not away in the midst of my days: * thy years are unto generation and generation.

segments.t: Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.

content.latin: 101:26 Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
content.english: 101:26 In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth: * and the heavens are the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.

content.latin: 101:27 Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.
content.english: 101:27 They shall perish but thou remainest: * and all of them shall grow old like a garment:

segments.t: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.

content.latin: 101:28 Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: 101:28 And as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed. * But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

segments.t: Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.

content.latin: 101:29 Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.
content.english: 101:29 The children of thy servants shall continue: * and their seed shall be directed for ever.

segments.t: Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.

content.latin: Ant. Clamor meus, Dómine, ad te pervéniat: non avértas fáciem tuam a me.
content.english: Ant. Let my cry reach unto thee, O Lord: turn not away thy face from me.

segments.t: Ant.
Clamor meus, Dómine, ad te pervéniat: non avértas fáciem tuam a me.

content.latin: Fratres: Iam non estis hóspites et ádvenæ: sed estis cives Sanctórum et doméstici Dei: superædificáti super fundaméntum Apostolórum, et Prophetárum, ipso summo angulári lápide Christo Iesu.
content.english: Brothers: Now therefore you are no more strangers and foreigners; but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and the domestics of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.

content.latin: ℣. Constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: ℣. Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: ℟. Mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.
content.english: ℟. They shall remember thy name, O Lord.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Esto, Dómine, plebi tuæ sanctificátor et custos: ut, Apóstoli tui Iacóbi muníta præsídiis, et conversatióne tibi pláceat, et secúra mente desérviat.
content.english: Be Thou thyself, O Lord, the Sanctifier and the Shepherd of thy people, that we who are overshadowed by the help of thine Apostle James may, in our conversation, walk with thee, and in all quietness of spirit serve thee.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
